newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Lion Teck Chiang expects relisting in 1H.
newsitem.headline: Lion Teck Chiang expects relisting in 1H.

text.p: Lion Teck Chiang Ltd (LTC), formerly known as Malaysian Feedmills Ltd (MFL), said on Thursday it expected to be relisted on the Stock Exchange of Singapore before the end of June.
The company said in a statement it had received approval from the High Court of Singapore for its share capital to be reduced in a restructuring of its business.
"Following the High Court approval, LTC is expected to be re-listed within the first half of 1997," it said.
Malaysia's Lion Group is pumping Singapore S$140 million of assets into LTC in a rescue of the loss-making MFL, a former producer of animal feed and agricultural products.
LTC, the new company formed in place of MFL will be involved in property and steel business.
LTC said a total of 32.5 million shares, made up of nine million new shares and 23.5 million vendor shares, will be offered through a public offer and a restricted offer.
The company had previously said the restricted offer will be 12 million shares to existing MFL shareholders on the basis of four shares for every one share held.
The price for all offer shares will be determined at a later date, the statement said.
After the restructuring and share offer, the Lion Group will emerge as the controlling shareholder with a 71.7 percent interest, the statement said.
A new board of directors has been appointed, with Cheng Theng Kee as chairman and Lionel Cheng as managing director, Sam Chong Keen as executive vice chairman and chief executive officer.
